source: All-In Podcast — GPT-5 underwhelms, AI TAM/ROIC/energy, China's advantage, tariffs, Nvidia chip smuggling, Apple buybacks and AI strategy
summary: Grok 4 represents a larger generational leap than GPT-5, marking the first time OpenAI has failed to release a decisively superior model after a competitor's frontier release.
summary_extended: Baker argues that Grok 4 represents the first meaningful generational leap by a competitor that OpenAI has failed to decisively surpass, marking a structural shift in frontier AI competitive dynamics. He supports this with specific benchmark data from Artificial Analysis showing Grok 4 scoring 44.4% on Humanity's Last Exam versus GPT-5's 42%, with Grok 4 also significantly outperforming on ARC-AGI-2. Baker attributes this competitive shift partly to talent attrition at OpenAI, suggesting the gap may not be a one-off result but a durable change in the competitive landscape. The investment implication is that xAI (Grok's developer, privately held) is gaining ground on OpenAI (also private), but neither company is US-listed, making this thesis primarily a qualitative signal about AI competitive dynamics rather than a directly actionable public equity trade.
